news.title: Egypt step up short-stature football preparations for Rabat World Cup · SNA
news.lede: Egypt's short-stature football team is due to begin a closed training camp in early November ahead of the World Cup in Rabat. Contribution SNA · Author profile · 31/10/2026 20:04 UTC. Egypt's short-stature football team are training in Cairo ahead of the World Cup scheduled for November in Rabat. They are due to enter a closed training camp in early November, then continue their preparations until they leave for Morocco.

news.title: Bangladesh reach U-15 World Cup quarterfinals in Tier E
news.lede: Bangladesh continued their winning run at FIFA’s inaugural U-15 World Cup and Festival, beating Singapore 4-3 on penalties to reach the quarterfinals in Tier E in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Wednesday. The last 16 fixture at the Hovsan Competition Complex ended 1-1 after regulation time before Bangladesh prevailed in the shootout to secure a place in the last eight. Earlier in the day, Akbar Hossain Ridon’s side had also needed penalties to overcome Seychelles in the last 32. After a 1-1 draw, Bangladesh won the shootout 4-2.

news.title: Boycotts, bans and no-shows: Notable World Cup absentees
news.lede: The first World Cup was hosted by Uruguay in 1930 and featured 13 teams, just four of which were from Europe: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. The paucity of European teams wasn't due to a boycott but largely had to do with funds being short during the Great Depression and the difficulty of traveling such a long distance by sea. It would be linked to a boycott at the next World Cup. Italy both hosted and won their first World Cup in 1934.

news.title: U15 football World Cup: Luxembourg finish 68th in first-ever World Cup appearance, above France
news.lede: The Luxembourg U15 squad concluded its U15 World Cup campaign in Azerbaijan with a 68th-place finish, following a 5-3 defeat to Scotland in its final game. The Luxembourg Football Federation (FLF) U15 squad finished in 68th place at the U15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, marking the first time a Luxembourg national football team has participated in a World Cup. The event, held in Baku, featured 189 nations competing in an eight-a-side format on smaller pitches with two 20-minute halves. https://www.facebook.com/photo? fbid=1805179617685620&set=a.600628604807400In the group stage, the team recorded four wins and one loss, finishing third in Group Q.
